title: Introduction to program-defined (user-defined) types
recap: A program-defined type gives a domain concept its own identity rather than only another name for a built-in type. Structs and enumerations are two important ways to define such types.
A small value type can make units explicit in an API. Passing and returning Money communicates cents without relying solely on parameter names.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: The supplied Money struct represents integer cents. Implement addMoney(left,right), returning a new Money containing the sum. Negative amounts are allowed. Do not mutate either input. Tested sums fit int. Return the program-defined type, not a plain int.
hints: Construct a Money result from the sum.
The value parameters are copies; callers should remain unchanged.
